Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Revenue collection via digital payments is supported: Côte d'Ivoire's DGI e-impôts portal enables online tax filing and payment, indicating government revenue collection through digital channels.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed by direct fetch of e-impôts (DGI): official portal for télédéclaration/télépaiement covering income tax, property tax (impôt foncier) and simplified tax registration for non-resident firms, with mobile-payment receipt download. Customs duties specifically are handled by a separate Douanes system not evidenced here, but the core claim (taxes payable digitally) is well supported. Value Code 3 (Yes) confirmed; still only one source type (DGI website itself), so corroboration on customs coverage is recommended.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system enables or plans to enable instant payments across national borders to other countries or regional payment systems, supporting remittances, trade, and regional integration.
Comments: Cross-border transfers exist via mobile money and regional systems: CGAP notes cross-border transfers are more prevalent in Côte d'Ivoire than in other markets and that MNOs have bilateral arrangements enabling cross-border transfers; this indicates partial cross-border functionality (not a single fully unified pan-African instant rail evidenced for all users).
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Refreshed and confirmed: Orange Money Côte d'Ivoire's live tariff/service pages (verified 2026) show operational cross-border send/receive with Senegal, Mali, Burkina Faso, Guinea-Bissau, Benin, Togo and Niger, and World Bank Remittance Prices data (2024) tracks the CIV-Mali corridor. BCEAO's Annual Report 2024 confirms the union-wide instant payment system (PI-SPI) is still only in pilot phase (launched July 2024) and Côte d'Ivoire is not yet a live PAPSS participant (PAPSS network coverage list, mid-2026, omits Côte d'Ivoire). This is genuine but limited/private-operator cross-border functionality rather than a fully operational public instant-payment rail, so Value Code 4 (Partially functional) remains the best fit, now on fresher, better-sourced evidence.

Definition: Whether the instant payment system is used or can be used for government disbursements to citizens, including social transfers, welfare payments, salaries, pensions, subsidies, grants, and emergency assistance.
Comments: Government-to-person payments are in active use: an IFC field note on Côte d'Ivoire digital social payments describes social safety net transfers delivered using a mobile money-based payment mechanism, reaching hundreds of thousands of beneficiaries.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Strongly confirmed and updated with much fresher evidence: a June 2025 government launch event reported 300,000 households (of a planned 527,000) receiving quarterly cash transfers (36,000 FCFA) via mobile money under the Filets Sociaux Productifs programme, alongside a new unified social registry (Régime Social Unique). A July 2024 ENSEA evaluation reports 402,000 households benefited 2017-2024, with 94% of digital payments delivered on time. Value Code 3 (Yes - Active Use) confirmed with high confidence.

Definition: Whether the system enables consumer payments to merchants and businesses for goods and services, including retail purchases, bill payments, e-commerce, and subscription services.
Comments: Mobile money in Côte d'Ivoire supports merchant payments (P2B); CGAP notes providers are experimenting with merchant payments and lists payments (including bills) as a dominant use case. (Evidence shows availability, not necessarily universal acceptance.)
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and refreshed: BCEAO's 2024 annual digital financial services report (UEMOA-wide, of which Côte d'Ivoire is the largest market) records merchant acceptance points more than doubling from 1,752,454 (2023) to 3,705,726 (2024), driven by QR-code deployment campaigns. This corroborates merchant payments being a live, growing use case. Value Code 2 (Yes) confirmed; the underlying data is regional (UEMOA) rather than Côte d'Ivoire-specific, so a country-level breakdown would strengthen the evidence further.

Comments: Person-to-government payments are in active use: Côte d'Ivoire's DGI operates the e-impôts portal for online tax filing and payment ("télédéclaration et télépaiement des impôts"), enabling taxpayers to complete tax formalities online.

revision_notes: Confirmed by direct fetch: the e-impôts portal has a dedicated space for individuals/professionals to view tax notices (avis d'imposition) and download proof of mobile payment, evidencing active P2G use, not merely capability. Value Code 3 (Yes - Active Use) confirmed.

Comments: Mobile money in Côte d'Ivoire supports person-to-person transfers; CGAP notes P2P money transfers have been the single biggest use case driving mobile money use in Côte d'Ivoire.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed with a fresher corroborating source: BCEAO's 2024 digital financial services report shows e-money accounts across UEMOA (Côte d'Ivoire's own currency union) growing 19% year-on-year to 248 million in 2024, consistent with continued, large-scale P2P mobile money use. Value Code 2 (Yes) confirmed; original CGAP evidence (2019) is dated but the underlying claim is not disputed by newer data.

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: BCEAO directly manages/operates key UEMOA payment systems used in Côte d'Ivoire. BCEAO states it is responsible for the management of SICA-UEMOA and STAR-UEMOA and performs operational, technical, and risk management activities (supervision, incident handling, reporting, invoicing, security, continuity, guarantee fund), indicating direct operation rather than only regulation.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and strengthened: BCEAO's 2010 Statutes and 2024 Annual Report confirm the Central Bank both governs (via its Board of Directors) and directly operates SICA-UEMOA and STAR-UEMOA, and in 2024 itself launched the pilot of the new WAEMU instant payment system (PI-SPI), which it also operates. Value Code 5 (Direct Operation) confirmed with primary, authoritative sources.

Comments: Côte d'Ivoire has a general data protection law: Law No. 2013-450 on protection of personal data, with ARTCI as the enforcement authority (general data protection coverage; not specific payment-data provisions identified in consulted sources).

revision_notes: Confirmed with the primary legal text and the regulator's own page (ARTCI), replacing the earlier aggregator source (dataprotection.africa, last updated 2022). Value Code 2 (General Data Protection Legislation) confirmed.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: BCEAO publishes regular statistical reporting that includes Côte d'Ivoire (e.g., Quarterly Statistical Bulletin, 4Q2024), indicating at least quarterly public reporting on monetary/financial indicators. However, a specific recurring public KPI report dedicated to PI-SPI performance (e.g., uptime, transaction volumes) was not identified in sources reviewed.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Revised down: the dedicated payment-system performance publication is BCEAO's "Rapport sur les Infrastructures de Marchés Financiers, les Moyens et les Services de Paiement" (covering the 2022-2023 period, published 2025) and the "Rapport annuel sur les services financiers numériques dans l'UEMOA" (explicitly annual, 2024 edition with detailed transaction/participant/merchant statistics). Neither is monthly or quarterly. The original citation (BCEAO Quarterly Statistical Bulletin) is a general monetary/financial statistics publication, not a payment-system performance report, so it does not support the Monthly/Quarterly tier. Value Code revised from 4 (Monthly/Quarterly) to 3 (Annual).

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: Share of adults with an account (financial institution or mobile money) is 51% in 2021 per World Bank Global Findex indicator for Côte d'Ivoire; using this as a proxy for active digital payment users implies 50-69% bracket.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Confirmed and refreshed with Global Findex 2025 (2024 survey data): the World Bank's country snapshot shows an adult population of 18.30 million with 7.77 million lacking an account, implying account ownership of approximately 57.5%; a separate Findex-derived indicator puts "digital payment adoption" at 56.5% for 2024. Both estimates sit within the 50-69% band. Note the Findex "digital payments" measure is a past-year, not strictly past-90-day, measure, so this is a reasonable but imperfect proxy for the variable's stricter 90-day definition. Value Code 3 (50-69%) confirmed.
